points.description: States that the STAR operator returns an alias/synonym (উপনাম) of the object that the operand points to — i.e. another name for that same object, not a copy of the object and not the pointer itself. Accept equivalent wording such as 'the object-এর একটি alias/synonym'. Do not accept 'returns the value stored at the address' as equivalent to alias for full marks.
points.partial_credit: Full 3 marks for alias/synonym of the pointed-to object; 2 marks if it says it returns/refers to the pointed-to object but does not make clear that the result is an alias/synonym; 1 mark if it only vaguely says it gets a value/object through the pointer without identifying the pointed-to object as the thing aliased.

levels.says: Says the STAR operator returns/refers to the object pointed to, but does not clearly state that the result is an alias/synonym of that object.
Only vaguely says it gets a value/object through the pointer, without identifying the pointed-to object as the thing aliased.

points.description: Identifies the operand of the STAR operator as a pointer/address that points to an object in memory. Accept equivalent wording such as 'operand-টি মেমোরিতে একটি object-এর দিকে নির্দেশ করে'.
Names the STAR operator as the dereferencing operator (or indirection operator); accept 'dereferencing operator' / 'ডিরেফারেন্সিং অপারেটর'.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all three ideas: the result is an alias/synonym of the pointed-to object, the operand is a pointer/address to that object in memory, and the STAR operator is the dereferencing operator. Part marks are available on P1 for answers that identify the pointed-to object but do not make clear that the result is an alias/synonym. Answers that describe only multiplication or pointer declaration, or that say it returns a copy of the object, earn no marks on P1.
